content: The Stockholm South Central Hospital and the Karolinska Institutet in Stockholm, Sweden, are key institutions involved in this work. Dr. Roopan Gill, a consultant in the Preventing Unsafe Abortion Unit of the Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) Department at the World Health Organization (WHO) in Geneva, Switzerland, also serves as a Women’s Health Advisor for Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) in Paris, France. Yelena Korotkaya is a Family Planning Fellow at the University of California, Los Angeles, USA. Dr. Lemi Tolu, an Assistant Professor of Obstetrics and Gynaecology at Saint Paul’s Hospital Millennium Medical College in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, is also a Family Planning Fellow. The Cochrane Response team includes lead researchers Nicholas Henschke, Yanina Sguassero, and Gemma Villanueva, with search strategy support provided by Elise Cogo. Team members and review authors include Hanna Bergman, Brian Buckley, Jennifer Petkovic, Chantelle Garritt, Candyce Hamel, and Katrin Probyn. WHO SRH staff, consultants, and Family Planning Fellows involved in this work include Dr. Ferid Abubeker, an Assistant Professor of Obstetrics and Gynaecology at Saint Paul’s Hospital Millennium Medical College in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia; Mekdes Feyssa, a Medical Officer in the Preventing Unsafe Abortion Unit at WHO in Geneva; and Dr. Roopan Gill, who also holds roles at WHO and MSF. Dr. Caron Kim, a Medical Officer in the same WHO unit, and Dr. Bianca Stifani, a Family Planning Fellow and Obstetrician-Gynaecologist at Albert Einstein College of Medicine and Montefiore Medical Center in New York, USA, are also contributors. Dr. Tesfaye Tufa, an Assistant Professor of Obstetrics and Gynaecology at Saint Paul’s Hospital Millennium Medical College in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, is another Family Planning Fellow involved. Other contributors include Professor Ernestina Coast from the London School of Economics and Political Science, UK, and Samantha Lattof, a Visiting Fellow in the Department of International Development at the same institution. Brittany Moore, a Consultant and Scientific and Technical Division Advisor at Ipas in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, USA, and Cheri Poss, Associate Director of Program Evidence at Ipas, are also part of the team. Professor Yana Rodgers from Rutgers University in New Brunswick, New Jersey, USA, specializes in women’s, gender, and sexuality studies and directs the Center for Women and Work. The Policy Surveillance Program at the Center for Public Health Law Research (CPHLR) at Temple University in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA, is led by Scott Burris, with team members including Lindsay Foster Cloud, Adrienne R. Ghorashi, Rachel Rebouché, and Patty Skuster. At Birmingham Law School, University of Birmingham, UK, Fiona de Londras, Chair of Global Legal Studies, leads the research team, which includes Alana Farrell and Magdalena Furgalska. The WHO Steering Group, chaired by the Department of Sexual and Reproductive Health and Research (SRH), led the guideline development process. This group included eight staff members from the department, seven of whom were from the Prevention of Unsafe Abortion (PUA) Unit. The group ensured that gender, ethics, social accountability, and human rights principles were integrated into the guidelines. They drafted the initial scope, identified priority questions in PICO format (Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcome), and selected individuals to participate as guideline methodologists and members of various evidence synthesis and review groups. The guideline methodologists worked closely with the WHO Steering Group and Evidence Synthesis Teams (ESTs) to appraise evidence using GRADE methodology. They oversaw methodological issues and conducted GRADE assessments of the evidence. The Steering Group also organized meetings, drafted recommendations, and finalized the guidelines in collaboration with external contributors. They monitored new information and user needs to determine when updates to the guidelines might be necessary. The group was supported by the wider WHO Secretariat, which included 19 staff members and consultants from the SRH Department and other WHO departments and regional offices.
